title: Dynamic signal prober for tokens/sec and p95 regression under mixed-tenant workloads
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: build a benchmark harness ("signal prober") that stresses the continuous-batching + queueing interaction under mixed-tenant and mixed-request-type traffic to surface tokens/sec throughput changes, p95 tail amplification, and silent regressions that only appear under realistic concurrency and priority mixes.

Rationale: earlier experiments show that simple homogeneous arrival patterns understate tail amplification when dynamic batching combines requests across tenants and priority classes. We need a deterministic harness that can: (1) reproduce pathologies observed on Dedicated pools, (2) quantify throughput vs. latency trade-offs across scheduling knobs, and (3) produce regression signals suitable for CI and nightly runs.

Scope and goals: produce a configurable harness that simulates: heterogeneous sequence lengths, chat vs. streaming generations, bursty arrival patterns, session affinity, and tenant priority classes. The harness must emit per-tenant tokens/sec, per-route p95/p99, batch size distribution, queue depth time-series, and a composite regression score (statistical test) that flags meaningful regressions.

Out-of-scope: full e2e customer traffic replay (this will be a synthetic prober); production rollout of automatic throttles (this ticket focuses on measurement and detection).
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run stable 3-hour mixed-tenant experiment with configurable proportions and arrival profiles
Metrics emitted to Grafana and Prometheus: tokens/sec (per-tenant), p50/p95/p99, batch-size histogram, queue depth histogram, KV cache hit ratio
Regression detector run on nightly baseline identifies regressions with false positive rate < 5% and true positive detection on injected degradations > 90%
A test-run README and config templates exist for: single-host small-scale, multi-host Dedicated-sim, and CI smoke run
Bench artifacts (CSV/Parquet) and a canonical Grafana dashboard link provided in the ticket
test_plan: Phase 0: local-mode smoke — validate harness produces stable metrics on a single inference worker (30m)
Phase 1: dedicated-sim — run 3 x 3-hour experiments varying tenant mixes (latency-sensitive vs throughput-sensitive), sequence lengths (64/512/2048), arrival patterns (Poisson, bursty, diurnal)
Phase 2: regression injection — introduce controlled kernel slowdown and 10% added queuing delay to validate detector sensitivity
Phase 3: CI integration — add a weekly job that runs a short 45m mixed run and computes the regression score against the baseline
initial_results_summary: Baseline small-scale run (2025-02-20):  aggregate tokens/sec 128k, median batch size 7, p95 72ms (low-concurrency mix)

Mixed-tenant run (2025-02-26): under 60/40 latency vs throughput tenant mix, tokens/sec fell 12% while p95 rose from 85ms -> 162ms at 95th percentile of background load; indicates tail amplification due to cross-tenant batching

Regression-injection run (2025-02-28): when adding 8ms kernel overhead we observed 24% increase in p95 for latency-sensitive tenant but only 6% drop in aggregate tokens/sec — detector flagged change with p < 0.01
notes:
Design choices: use workload compositor that samples from pre-defined request prototypes (short chat turn, long generation, streaming tokens) and a lightweight traffic controller that can vary inter-arrival distributions and tenant weights. Prefer deterministic RNG seeds for CI reproducibility.

Trade-offs: synthetic workloads give control but may miss some customer correlation patterns; will plan a follow-up to incorporate limited sanitized replay. Detector uses a combination of bootstrap confidence intervals and Mann-Whitney U test to avoid sensitivity to non-Gaussian tails.

Instrumentation: emit metrics using our standard telemetry library; batch and queue histograms must be labeled by model and tenant for drilldowns.
implementation_plan: Week 1: harness code scaffold + workload compositor + local smoke tests
Week 2: integrate telemetry + create Grafana dashboard + run dedicated-sim experiments
Week 3: implement statistical regression detector, run injection tests, tune thresholds
Week 4: CI job + docs + handoff to SRE for nightly runs
risks: Synthetic traffic may not capture deep real-world correlated failures
Resource consumption on Dedicated clusters during long runs could impact customer SLAs if misconfigured
False positives from detector during platform maintenance windows
mitigation: Add a 'maintenance window' filter for nightly jobs and baseline updates
Throttle harness runs on shared Dedicated pools; prefer isolated test pools or small scale
Schedule a follow-up to validate against sanitized replay traces from two pilot customers
